proof_summary: For \(p=2m+1\), Lucas congruences pair the \(k<p\) and \(k\ge p\) parts of each defining sum with opposite contributions, giving \(f(p+r)\equiv0\pmod p\) for \(0\le r<p\); at \(n=p-1\) they give \(a(p-1)\equiv1\) and \(c(p-1)\equiv(-1)^m\), since in the latter sum a central binomial factor vanishes except at \(k=m\). Thus both Hankel matrices are anti-triangular modulo \(p\), and column reversal evaluates their determinants as \((-1)^m f(p-1)^p=(-1)^m f(p-1)\), making the second reversal sign cancel while the first remains.
